The Newsroom AI Masterclass Series and Newsroom AI Catalyst support Ukraine’s independent news sector with a focus on AI adoption, innovation and resilience.

OpenAI, WAN-IFRA and the Association of Independent Regional Press Publishers of Ukraine (AIRPPU) have announced a new initiative to support and strengthen Ukrainian news publishers by building practical artificial intelligence capabilities and accelerating innovation across their organisations. highlights.title: England's push for 'world-class' all-rounders to close gap on Australia
highlights.summary: England Women's national selector Lydia Greenway laid out her plan for the side to close the gap on the world's best, Australia, with a push for 'world-class' allrounders at the heart of their strategy.
body: As part of that plan, all-rounders Dani Gibson and Freya Kemp have been starters throughout the summer, which included T20 series wins over New Zealand and India, as well as a run to the final of the T20 World Cup on home soil - before being beaten by Australia.
Charlotte Edwards' side were also well beaten by India in a historic first women's Test at Lord's, but they ended their summer on a high with a 3-0 ODI series sweep of Ireland.
"We don't want to be behind Australia all the time, we've got to close that gap," Greenway told Sky Sports Cricket during the third ODI win over Ireland on Sunday.
"And when you look at Australia, and how they're lined up in their top seven, they've probably got three or four bowling options - so we need to look at how we can do that.

highlights.title: France’s Halley Production Boards Thriller ‘Carro Seco,’ About Killer Who Targets Unscrupulous Barcelona Real Estate Speculators (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Paris-based Halley Production has boarded Javier Polo’s feature film thriller project “Carro Seco” (“Carreau”), showcased at the upcoming Iberseries & Platino Industria’s Co-Production and Financing Forum in Madrid.
body: Dressed like a vintage pétanque player, the vigilante is driven by the social impact of gentrification. Casting himself as a housing Robin Hood, he justifies his crimes as acts committed for the common good.
As two detectives navigate the investigation, public opinion splits between viewing the murderer as a heroic housing vigilante or a psychopath.

“‘Carro Seco’ uses the tension of a psychological thriller to address one of today’s most urgent social conflicts: silent evictions and real estate speculation,” says Polo. “What sets it apart is the contrast between that social nightmare and a unique, ritualistic iconography; turning an innocent neighborhood sport like pétanque into a deadly weapon accompanied by French chanson. It is a film that challenges the viewer with an uncomfortable moral dilemma about justice, boundaries, and empathy.”

Halley Production’s international co-productions include such cross-border hits as Javier Fesser’s 2018 crowd-pleaser “Champions,” Manuel Gómez Pereira’s 2025 Goya-winning Spanish hit “ The Dinner ” and the forthcoming drama “ Primo Viaggio.”

highlights.title: Is it true that … hard water damages hair?
highlights.summary: Mineral deposits can accumulate, making hair drier, but removing them can cause different problems. From hair treatments to shower filters, a wave of products have been launched promising to protect hair from the “problems” caused by living in a hard-water area. But are they really necessary?
body: When water moves through soil and rocks, such as limestone, minerals dissolve into it and remain there when it comes out of your tap. These minerals are responsible for the limescale that builds up in your kettle.

“You know you’re living in a hard‑water area by how easy it is to lather up soap,” says Tobin. “If it is really difficult, and it forms a kind of scum rather than bubbles, you’re in a hard-water area. It’s healthy to drink, but it can trigger some issues.”

Washing your hair in hard water can leave mineral deposits on the hair shaft, which some believe make it look duller and feel rougher. There is evidence that calcium and magnesium can accumulate on hair washed in hard water, although the evidence that this causes damage is less clear.

Removing this buildup can cause problems, though, especially for those with dry or brittle hair. Tobin says the best shampoos for doing so are high lather and contain ingredients such as sulfates, which can be harsh on those hair types. “It’s this balancing act between removing the buildup and leaving enough oil in the system to condition the hair,” says Tobin.

From hair treatments to shower filters, a wave of products have been launched promising to protect hair from the “problems” caused by living in a hard-water area.

highlights.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
highlights.summary: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.
body: Some authors hoping to receive their share of Anthropic’s $1.5 billion copyright settlement said they received surprising emails this week — emails informing them that someone else was making a claim on their payments.

Anthropic settled a copyright class action suit last year, after a judge ruled that training AI models on copyrighted material is legal under fair use doctrine, but pirating that material was not. The deal received final approval in July, allowing the payments to move forward.

Under the terms of the settlement, the authors of nearly 500,000 titles will be paid $3,000 for each pirated work. If the book is still in-print with a traditional publisher, the money will be split 50-50 between author and publisher. If the book was self-published, or if the publisher reverted the rights by allowing the book to go out-of-print, then the author should get the entire payment.

highlights.title: Pixel 11 review: Google sets the bar for standard flagship phones
highlights.summary: Longer battery life, faster chip, actually useful AI tools and better cameras keep quality Android ahead of competition. Google’s Pixel 11 continues to set the standard for what you should expect from the base model of a flagship phone with class-leading cameras, long software support and almost…
body: The regular Pixel 11 costs £879 (€999/$899/A$1,499) making it £80 or equivalent more expensive than last year’s model as the cost of RAMageddon continues to bite. It’s not cheap by any stretch of the imagination, but it comes with 256GB of storage and is £200 less than the Pixel 11 Pro, matching rival Samsung’s Galaxy S26.

At a glance the Pixel 11 looks very similar to the previous two Google phone iterations: glass front and back with flat aluminium sides and large pill-shaped bar at the back, which is much slimmer this time. Stick it in a case and the protruding camera all but disappears.

The 6.3in OLED screen is crisp and super bright with up to a 120Hz refresh rate to keep your scrolling smooth. The in-screen fingerprint scanner is fast and accurate, while the camera-based face recognition works well during the day and is secure enough for use with banking apps, unlike similar systems on most Android rivals.

The Pixel has a new generation of Google’s chip, the Tensor G6, which is up to 20% faster in tests. It significantly lags top-end rivals from Qualcomm and Apple, so won’t win any raw performance awards, but feels snappy in daily tasks and can handle mid-level gaming just fine.

highlights.title: The NFL is back! The race to Super Bowl 61 starts here
highlights.summary: 285 games. Eight countries. Four continents. Six time zones. 22 weeks. 32 teams. One champion. And five gold rings - oops, sorry Jayden Daniels. The 2026 NFL season is here.
body: Seven months ago, discarded embers of confetti would pave the way for our meandering walk towards the exit at an emptying Levi's Stadium as the curtain closed on Super Bowl 60, footballing disciples reluctant to accept it was all over for another year as they braced for annual hibernation.

Sam Darnold had just crowned one of sport's great fairy-tale redemption stories, Aden Durde had just made British sporting history, Mike Macdonald's Dark Side defense had just tormented Drake Maye and Bad Bunny had just delivered a clinic in reggaeton rage-bait in the face of orange-tinged white-housed backlash over his landmark half-time show.

Seattle Seahawks players and coaches alike rejoiced over childhood dreams fulfilled in the company of loved ones, while for others the clock had already reset, for football rarely dwells too long on the present.
The countdown is finally over. From here on, there shall be no more football-less Sundays until February. The road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles starts here.

highlights.title: Brandon Sanderson Reveals the Fatal Fantasy Mistake That Derailed Game of Thrones
highlights.summary: Brandon Sanderson is one of the biggest voices in the fantasy genre. More than a writer and publisher, he's an audience-friendly scholar. Somehow he finds time to expand the Cosmere on a near-annual basis and also deliver lectures on Tolkien’s magic systems.
body: In a talk with fellow fantasy author Joe Abercrombie, shared on YouTube earlier this year, the pair discussed the craft of writing. That’s when Game of Thrones was brought up — again. For Sanderson, it is a prime example of the strengths and weaknesses of Epic Fantasy.

"I grew up reading the big epics. I think it's the most natural form for fantasy in some ways. It gives you a lot of time to dig into that world and immerse yourself in it and explore another place,” he said. "I think that's why Game of Thrones did well."

When asked about the downside of these stories, Sanderson spoke from personal experience, sharing that burnout is a real problem, with him having to take a break from the writing process at around the 10th pass of the draft.

"Epic fantasy has this danger. It starts very personal, and then it can drift away from being personal about the characters if you're not careful. Authors tend to get more excited about side characters later on. We see this happening a bit in Game of Thrones and in A Wheel of Time. How can you make sure something that big remains fresh and personal and exciting? That's a real challenge with the genre."
points: Brandon Sanderson is one of the biggest voices in the fantasy genre.
More than a writer and publisher, he's an audience-friendly scholar.

highlights.title: Going for gold: an early autumn road trip across Finland’s sparkling lake district
highlights.summary: On a self-drive break in search of Lake Saimaa’s autumn colours, we encountered blue skies, cosy lakeside cabins and saunas, great food – and lots of stubbornly green trees.
body: I wasn’t sure what to expect from an autumn trip to Finland, my first ever to the country, but spending an afternoon sprawled on a deck chair beneath blazing blue skies certainly wasn’t part of it. After a morning walking beneath the leafy canopy at the Mustila Arboretum – the oldest, most extensive botanical garden in the country – and a lunchtime wine-tasting (more of which later), my friend Sara and I pitched up at the Sahanlahti resort, deep in the Finnish Lakeland, only to find sun-drenched scenery that felt far more Mediterranean than Nordic.

Sahanlahti was the second stop on a mid-September road trip from Helsinki to the shores of Lake Saimaa; a journey in search of ruska, the spectacular autumn colours that blaze for a few short weeks before the long Finnish winter sets in. However, on our opening drive east from the airport to the Radalla resort, set on Lake Urajärvi, most of the thousands of trees we drove past were resolutely green, with just the very tips of the leaves tinged with auburn, like a foliage balayage.

highlights.title: My Brief Summer Fling With Siri AI
highlights.summary: I was initially enamored with the beta version of Apple’s revamped smartphone assistant. As the full release approaches, I’ve forgotten Siri AI even exists.
body: When I first tested the developer beta of Apple's Siri AI by taking it as my tour guide around San Francisco, I was convinced the overhauled smartphone assistant would be an “ everything tool ” on the iPhone. The answers felt reliable enough and more helpful than previous versions of Siri. Also, the chatbot-style app for Siri felt very sleek, very Apple-y.

Over the next month, I kept experimenting with the Siri AI in the iOS 27 beta. The tool was quite powerful, especially with the personal context brought in by indexing the contents of my phone. Finding an ancient text message or photo has never been easier. Even so, my usage of the smartphone assistant slowly started tapering off.

It’s not that Siri AI isn’t better now. It is! This new version is quite the step change, which makes my reaction even more devastating. Siri AI isn’t revolutionizing how I interact with my phone the way I'd initially hoped, especially as an AI assistant built directly into the device and factoring in that Apple gives more thought to preserving my privacy than many other AI companies.

The hosts are looking to earn their first outright victory since their famous 15-13 away success in 2021, having scrambled a dramatic 14-14 tie to retain in Spain in 2023 before Team USA secured a 15.5-12.5 victory the following year.

World No 1 Nelly Korda headlines Team USA and is a two-time major winner this season, with captain Angela Stanford now looking to lead the visitors to their first away success in the biennial contest since 2015.

highlights.title: A new start after 60: I was always quiet – but at 82 I’m a famous, funny fashion influencer
highlights.summary: Vivienne Truran was a civil servant and antiques dealer, who spent most of her life in the background. At 80, she realised how outgoing she was, and started a soaringly successful new career. ‘It took me till I was 80 to realise that I’m quite an outgoing and loud person,” says Vivienne Truran.
body: It all started 18 months ago. “I think I want to be an influencer,” she announced in one of her first reels. “Now, what can I influence people in?”

Wasn’t Truran outgoing when she was younger? “No,” she says. “My husband, Martin, was 6ft 4in. Rugby player, good-looking chap. When he walked into the room, he took the room. So I, like a good wife, was in the background. You can’t have two noisy people in a relationship. It doesn’t work.”

They were happily married for more than 40 years; but Martin got dementia and had a number of strokes, and died in hospital during Covid. Truran has no children, and no siblings. Feeling isolated, she would make a cake and sometimes take a piece to her then neighbour – now talent manager – James Rolling, and they became friends. It was Rolling who persuaded her to get in front of the camera.

He introduced her to his friends as his carer, for a joke; hence her Instagram tag @vivthecarer. They “respect each other and are a good team”, Truran says, but if she could change her tag, she would be “Viv from the Vale … like Jenny from the block”. She describes herself as a “timeless fashionista”, which she says is her third career.

highlights.title: Why China Is the Bogeyman Data Center Enthusiasts Just Can't Quit
highlights.summary: Polls show that overwhelming majorities of Americans hate data centers. China makes a perfect scapegoat for tech leaders and their allies—the only problem is a lack of evidence.
body: Welcome to the first edition of Power Play! From now until the midterms, senior writer Molly Taft will be sharing their thoughts every Sunday on this political season’s hottest issue: data centers. We welcome reader comments, and will be answering questions from the comments section in future editions.

Be sure to catch WIRED’s first livestream on data centers this Thursday, September 10, featuring Molly, senior politics correspondent Hugo Lowell, and senior business writer Max Zeff! You can submit questions here.

It’s been a rough summer for data center boosters. Polling is getting even more dismal—as many as 75 percent of Americans now say they would oppose a data center being built in their area, up from 42 percent last year. Politicians from both parties who were previously advocates, like Texas governor Greg Abbott and Pennsylvania governor Josh Shapiro, are now switching up as the midterms approach, looking to convey to voters that they’re talking a hard line on the hated infrastructure.

highlights.title: Designers should not fear being replaced by AI, industry leaders say
highlights.summary: Firms are more likely to use technology as ‘the intern in the office’ than as a replacement for skilled staff. Professional designers should not feel “threatened” by the rapid growth of generative AI, according to business leaders, despite fears over job losses in the sector.
body: With design and film production companies and manufacturers all adopting AI at an accelerating pace, industry bodies said the technology would be used to enhance the work of designers rather than replace them.
Mat Hunter, the chief executive of the Design Council – a charity which champions the industry – said that while AI was increasingly being used by designers, “they are using it to add value”.

He said: “We are aware that technology always displaces people with new ways of working. However, we believe in the imagination and inventiveness of designers to find opportunities. We believe the UK needs more professional designers, so overall employment should continue to grow.”

Deborah Dawton, chief executive of the Design Business Council, said: “What protects great designers from AI is skill, experience, empathy and deep understanding of the sectors they operate in. So, no, [workers] shouldn’t feel threatened if they operate at this level.”

highlights.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is one of, if not the best, RPGs of all time. 11 years after launch, there's even a remastered version of it coming later this month (and it's free for anyone who owns the existing game), alongside a new expansion called Songs of the Past that's in the works.
body: The Witcher 3 has plenty of defining traits: a beautiful, dense open world; side quests with narratives so enrapturing they're better than most games' main stories; larger-than-life characters who become so personable, you'd consider them friends; and combat mechanics that allow you to dance between foes, all while using two swords and magic at once.
If any of that sounds like your sort of thing, here are the eight best games like The Witcher 3.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is the newest game on this list, and it comes from studio Rebel Wolves, which is led by The Witcher 3 game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz. The studio also employs a number of other former high-level staffers from CD Projekt Red, and as a result, it's one of the closest games you'll find to matching what Geralt's best adventure has to offer.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, you are Coen. He's part-vampire, part-witch, a.k.a. a Dawnwalker. Not a Witcher. Structurally, however, this is heavily inspired by The Witcher games: a stunning open world with so many side quests to find, innovative, direction-based, parry-focused combat, and a unique time-based mechanic where every decision truly matters.

highlights.title: An Alien Mind
highlights.summary: Jakub Pachocki reflects on increasingly capable AI and the challenge of keeping it aligned. He calls for stronger safeguards and international coordination.
body: In mid-2023, within the “RLSlow” research project, we saw the first results that gave us confidence that we will be able to scale the training of reasoning models, unlocking the capability of pretrained models to form their own chains of thought. Szymon and I spent that night at the office, thinking not about the incredible benchmark numbers, products, or scientific results that this technology will deliver - but rather, trying to process the sobering fact we will actually see machines meaningfully smarter than ourselves in our lifetime, and we already see the shape of these systems; wondering how to alert people to the significance of this.

Three years later, reasoning language models are a rapidly growing part of the economy and starting to push the boundaries of science. They are able to operate computers and graphical interfaces, collaborate with people and each other, and carry out research projects. They are also transforming the landscape of computer security, and in that present clear new dangers.

highlights.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4 Review & Recap: "The Weenie"
highlights.summary: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain. Read our full review.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4!

Lanterns sure left us hanging these past couple of weeks, ending Episode 2 with the debut of Ulrich Thomsen’s Sinestro and then pivoting away to tell a flashback storyline in Episode 3 ( a great flashback storyline, but a flashback all the same). Only now in Episode 4 do we see the full reunion between Sinestro and his former protege. It’s a definite high point of the episode, albeit an all too brief one.

I feel similarly about the other key GL villain introduced in Episode 4, Jason Manuel Olazábal’s Hector Hammond. We basically get one good, solid sequence out of Hector and that’s it. The standoff between Hector and Hal/John (Aaron Pierre) is tense and stressful in the best way, but it’s also over very quickly. At that point, we learn that Hector is really just Hector Gutiérrez, another fakeout used by the Manhunter to throw our heroes off their scent. And unlike Sinestro, there’s not even any prior history between Hal and Hector in this universe. This is a major DC villain who’s being effectively wasted as a one-off misdirection.
points: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain.

body: For AGI to benefit all of humanity, we believe it must be democratically governed. This can only happen through an informed public debate about the capabilities, risks and safeguards of highly capable AI systems. People everywhere need to understand the likely future trajectory of frontier AI, so they can have a meaningful voice in how it develops.

highlights.summary: With many emerging local designers showing outside of TFW, the SS27 schedule felt sparse. But this season, JFWO seized the opportunity to showcase international talent.
body: When you incubate and support local talent you hope will reach global relevance, how can you keep reaping the rewards?

That’s the question that Japan Fashion Week Organization (JFWO) is wrestling with this season, as Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo evaluates its standing as a springboard for emerging designers — who are increasingly springing away. With many of its biggest names moving off schedule or showing abroad, the event must look elsewhere to maintain relevance.

The week nevertheless remains a reliable arena to scout for talent, as new designers enter the fashion week system through a combined effort of awards systems and a fresh international push. Here’s what you missed from the week.

There were 27 shows on the main schedule across six days, but many of Tokyo’s biggest domestic designers were absent, having either opted to showcase their collections via lookbook shoots or to hold off-schedule shows earlier in the season, usually in order to be closer to the men’s schedule or to the pre-summer buying season in Paris.

Not you -- even though you bought it -- but them. They also talk about knowing everybody in the household, knowing the secondary devices, moving from TVs to smartphones and other screens, and more in their B2B discussions. Beyond just the fact that we think the TV's native behavior parallels malware, the LG Smart TVs we tested also have a number of security vulnerabilities that can be exploited to convert the TVs into covert listening devices. In this investigation, we dive into the mix of LG's first-party functionality that (in our opinions) is tantamount to spying and LG's vulnerabilities and exploits that they have failed to protect against.
